text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Vice-president Professor George Saitoti shuns a reconciliation move by embattled rival William ole Ntimama.
- Police are investigating for a possible link between three people found at the Ngong forest a day before the bodies of the two policemen brutally murdered and bodies dumped at the forest.
- Finance minister Musalia Mudavadi waives duty on essential commodities as famine tightens its grip on parts of the country.
- Uchumi Supermarket incurred a loss of 400 million shillings ($7.4 million) in the fierce fire that razed its chain of warehouses in Nairobi's Industrial Area over the weekend.
- Initiators of peace talks between the Kikuyu and Kalenjin communities will soon meet to discuss the possible revival of talks between the two following the 1990-94 tribal animosity and clashes.
- A secondary school teacher allegedly beat his wife to death after she asked for money to buy their child milk.
- Four opposition parliamentarians insist that opposition chairman Michael Kijana Wamalwa should resign to save the opposition from further disgrace.
- Wanted criminal Bernard "Rasta" Matheri Thuo has been spotted in Nairobi.
- Kenya is declared free from the guinea-worm disease by the World Health Organisation.
